subject: Request: SAML assertion traces & access‑review snapshots for SOC 2 Type II review
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Peter Liu <peter.liu@medicorelabs.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SAML assertion traces & access‑review snapshots for SOC 2 Type II review

Hi Peter —

Thanks again for sending the SOC 2 Type II report last week. We're starting our internal mapping against your report and a few downstream customers have asked us to validate specific control evidence to close out their SIG/SOC questionnaires. To avoid back-and-forth later, can you help with the following artifacts scoped to your audit period (2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31):

1) SAML assertion traces: an extract of the SAML assertion logs (assertion ID, Issuer, Subject, Recipient, AuthnInstant, AssertionConsumerServiceURL, Status) for all successful front-channel SSO events during the audit window. Ideally CSV.

2) Admin/privileged action logs from your IdP (Okta/Azure AD): a slice showing role/grant changes, application assignments, and admin MFA policy edits during the period. Include actor, target, action, timestamp.

3) Access review exports: the last completed access recertification run that overlaps the audit window (CSV or spreadsheet with reviewer, review outcome, scope).

4) MFA enforcement evidence: a snapshot showing enforcement policy and a sample of user enrollment dates (redact emails if needed).

We do not need full PII — hashed IDs or pseudonyms are fine — but the logs must contain timestamps and the fields above so our auditors can confirm control activity.

Attached is the Type II report you shared (for reference) and a short spec listing the required SAML fields (saml_assertion_trace_spec.txt). If you can provide these as exports or a shared Drive link, that would be ideal.

Can you confirm whether you can share these by COB Wednesday, 2026-03-31? If that timeline is tight we can partition the ask (SAML traces first, then admin logs).

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Security & Compliance Program Manager | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0124
From: Peter Liu <peter.liu@medicorelabs.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SAML assertion traces & access‑review snapshots for SOC 2 Type II review

Logan —

Thanks for the clear list. We can supply most of this but need to clarify two items so we deliver exactly what you need:

• Audit window: you call out 2025-07-01 → 2025-12-31. Do you need inclusive timestamps in UTC? We can provide both UTC and local timestamps.

• SAML fields: our IdP records extensive XML. Do you need the raw XML assertions or a flattened CSV with the specific fields you listed? Our default is to export XML; we can run a transform and provide a CSV.

We'll prepare a sample CSV slice (50 rows) for your review before exporting the full set.

I can commit to delivering the sample by EOD today and the full slices by 2026-03-31, pending internal approvals for the admin action logs.

— Peter
Peter Liu
Security Engineer | Medicore Labs
pet er.liu@medicorelabs.com

Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SAML assertion traces & access‑review snapshots for SOC 2 Type II review

Peter —

UTC timestamps are best for the audit; a flattened CSV is preferred (our auditors want the field columns visible). The 50-row sample is perfect — thanks. For the admin logs, if you anticipate needing DPA/additional approvals, please flag so we can loop legal early.

One other small ask: can you include a brief bridge note if any of the exports are generated from a different system than what was assessed in the Type II report (we'll surface that to our auditor).

Thanks again.

— Logan
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: quick question on minimum schema

Logan —

For the SAML CSV we should validate presence of: assertion_id, issuer, subject_id (pseudonym ok), authn_instant (UTC), recipient, acs_url, nameid_format, status_code. Also we prefer a field called "raw_xml_reference" (GUID) so auditor can request a sample of raw XML without giving full assertions.

I'm happy to run a quick schema check on the sample once Peter shares it.

— Olga
Engineering Manager, Identity Systems
